requirements.title: Establishment of a risk management system
requirements.obligation: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: Applies to every high‑risk AI system
requirements.machine_constraint: System must contain a documented risk‑management plan that is kept up‑to‑date throughout the product lifecycle
evidence_expected: Risk management system documentation
Version‑controlled records of updates
requirements.source_quote: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.

requirements.title: Continuous, iterative risk management process
requirements.obligation: Operate the risk management system as a continuous iterative process with regular systematic review and updating throughout the entire lifecycle
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems, across design, development, deployment and post‑market phases
requirements.machine_constraint: Risk‑management process must be scheduled to execute periodic reviews (e.g., at least annually) and incorporate updates based on new information
evidence_expected: Review logs
Update records showing timestamps and rationale
requirements.source_quote: The risk management system shall be understood as a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic review and updating.

requirements.title: Risk identification and analysis (step a)
requirements.obligation: Identify and analyze known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety or fundamental rights when used as intended
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Perform a documented risk‑identification activity covering all known and reasonably foreseeable scenarios aligned with the system’s intended purpose
evidence_expected: Risk identification report
Mapping of risks to health, safety or fundamental rights
requirements.source_quote: the identification and analysis of the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights when the high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose;

requirements.title: Risk estimation and evaluation (step b)
requirements.obligation: Estimate and evaluate risks that may emerge under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Apply quantitative or qualitative risk‑estimation methods to both intended‑use and reasonably foreseeable misuse scenarios
evidence_expected: Risk estimation matrices
Evaluation summaries for misuse cases
requirements.source_quote: the estimation and evaluation of the risks that may emerge when the high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose, and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse;

requirements.title: Post‑market risk evaluation (step c)
requirements.obligation: Evaluate other risks based on data gathered from the post‑market monitoring system (Article 72)
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Integrate post‑market monitoring data into periodic risk‑evaluation activities
evidence_expected: Post‑market monitoring data extracts
Risk evaluation reports referencing Article 72 data
requirements.source_quote: the evaluation of other risks possibly arising, based on the analysis of data gathered from the post-market monitoring system referred to in Article 72;

requirements.title: Adoption of targeted risk‑management measures (step d)
requirements.obligation: Adopt appropriate and targeted risk‑management measures to address identified risks
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Select and implement mitigation actions that map to each identified risk and are documented in the risk‑management plan
evidence_expected: Mitigation action list
Traceability matrix linking risks to measures
requirements.source_quote: the adoption of appropriate and targeted risk management measures designed to address the risks identified pursuant to point (a).

requirements.title: Scope of risks to be addressed
requirements.obligation: Consider only risks that can be reasonably mitigated or eliminated through design, development or provision of adequate technical information
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All risk‑management activities for high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Filter risk‑identification outputs to retain only those mitigable via design changes or technical documentation
evidence_expected: Justification why each risk is within the mitigable scope
requirements.source_quote: The risks referred to in this Article shall concern only those which may be reasonably mitigated or eliminated through the development or design of the high-risk AI system, or the provision of adequate technical information.

requirements.title: Residual risk acceptability
requirements.obligation: Ensure that residual risk for each hazard and the overall residual risk are judged to be acceptable
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: After implementation of risk‑management measures for high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Provide an acceptability assessment that demonstrates residual risk levels meet predefined acceptance criteria
evidence_expected: Residual risk assessment report
Acceptability criteria documentation
requirements.source_quote: The risk management measures referred to in paragraph 2, point (d), shall be such that the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard, as well as the overall residual risk of the high-risk AI systems is judged to be acceptable.

requirements.title: Testing to determine appropriate risk‑management measures
requirements.obligation: Test high‑risk AI systems to identify the most appropriate and targeted risk‑management measures, ensuring consistent performance for the intended purpose and compliance with this Section
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems before market placement or putting into service
requirements.machine_constraint: Execute defined test suites that generate evidence of compliance with intended‑purpose performance metrics and risk‑management requirements
evidence_expected: Test plans
Test reports showing metrics and thresholds
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be tested for the purpose of identifying the most appropriate and targeted risk management measures. Testing shall ensure that high-risk AI systems perform consistently for their intended purpose and that they are in compliance with the requirements set out in this Section.

requirements.title: Timing and criteria of testing
requirements.obligation: Perform testing at any time during development, and in any event prior to market placement, against prior‑defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to the intended purpose
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Maintain a repository of predefined performance metrics and probabilistic thresholds; verify test outcomes against them before release
evidence_expected: Metric definition documents
Proof that tests were run before market launch
requirements.source_quote: The testing of high-risk AI systems shall be performed, as appropriate, at any time throughout the development process, and, in any event, prior to their being placed on the market or put into service. Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.

requirements.title: Consideration of vulnerable persons
requirements.obligation: When implementing the risk management system, consider whether the system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under 18 and, where appropriate, other vulnerable groups
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: During risk‑management system design for all high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Include a vulnerability impact assessment covering minors (<18 years) and other identified vulnerable groups
evidence_expected: Vulnerability impact assessment report
Mitigation actions targeting identified vulnerable‑group risks
requirements.source_quote: When implementing the risk management system as provided for in paragraphs 1 to 7, providers shall give consideration to whether in view of its intended purpose the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups.

requirements.title: Integration with other Union law risk‑management processes
requirements.obligation: Allow the aspects of this Article to be part of or combined with internal risk‑management procedures established pursuant to other relevant Union law
requirements.actor: Provider of a high‑risk AI system subject to other Union law internal risk‑management requirements
requirements.applicability: When the provider already has internal risk‑management obligations under other Union legislation
requirements.machine_constraint: Document how the risk‑management activities required by this Article are mapped to or merged with existing Union‑law risk‑management processes
evidence_expected: Cross‑reference matrix between EU AI Act risk‑management steps and other Union law procedures
requirements.source_quote: For providers of high-risk AI systems that are subject to requirements regarding internal risk management processes under other relevant provisions of Union law, the aspects provided in paragraphs 1 to 9 may be part of, or combined with, the risk management procedures established pursuant to that law.

requirements.title: Use of data sets meeting quality criteria
requirements.obligation: Develop high‑risk AI systems that use model‑training techniques on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria listed in Articles 10(2)‑(4) and Article 4a(1).
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems employing techniques involving the training of AI models
requirements.machine_constraint: ∀ ds ∈ {training, validation, testing} : ds.meetsQualityCriteria == true  // criteria defined in Art10(2‑4) & Art4a(1)
evidence_expected: data‑set quality assessment report
mapping to Article 4a(1) compliance checklist
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria referred to in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of this Article and in Article 4a(1) whenever such data sets are used.

requirements.title: Adopt appropriate data governance and management practices
requirements.obligation: Implement data governance and management practices appropriate to the intended purpose of the high‑risk AI system, covering design choices, data collection, preparation, assumptions, availability assessment, bias examination, bias mitigation, and data‑gap identification.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataGovernance.practiceSet ⊇ {designChoices, collectionInfo, preparationOps, assumptions, availabilityAssessment, biasExamination, biasMitigation, gapIdentification}
evidence_expected: data governance policy document
record of design decisions affecting data

requirements.title: Consider relevant design choices in data governance
requirements.obligation: Take into account relevant design choices affecting the data sets during data governance.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataGovernance.considersDesignChoices == true
evidence_expected: design‑choice impact analysis on data
requirements.source_quote: (a) the relevant design choices;

requirements.title: Document data collection processes and origin
requirements.obligation: Document data collection processes, data origin, and for personal data the original purpose of collection.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.collectionInfo.recorded == true && (if DataSet.containsPersonalData => DataSet.originalPurpose.recorded == true)
evidence_expected: metadata registry of data sources and collection purpose
requirements.source_quote: (b) data collection processes and the origin of data, and in the case of personal data, the original purpose of the data collection;

requirements.title: Record data‑preparation operations
requirements.obligation: Maintain records of data‑preparation operations such as annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.preparationLog.containsAll {annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment, aggregation}
evidence_expected: data‑preparation log or provenance metadata
requirements.source_quote: (c) relevant data-preparation processing operations, such as annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation;

requirements.title: Formulate and document assumptions about data
requirements.obligation: Formulate and document assumptions regarding what the data are intended to measure and represent.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.assumptionsDocumented == true
evidence_expected: assumptions statement linked to each data set
requirements.source_quote: (d) the formulation of assumptions, in particular with respect to the information that the data are supposed to measure and represent;

requirements.title: Assess availability, quantity and suitability of data sets
requirements.obligation: Perform an assessment of the availability, quantity and suitability of the data sets required for the system.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.availabilityAssessment.completed == true && DataSet.quantityAssessment.completed == true && DataSet.suitabilityAssessment.completed == true
evidence_expected: availability and adequacy assessment report
requirements.source_quote: (e) an assessment of the availability, quantity and suitability of the data sets that are needed;

requirements.title: Examine potential biases affecting health, safety, fundamental rights or discrimination
requirements.obligation: Examine data sets for biases that could affect health and safety, fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, especially when data outputs influence future inputs.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: BiasAnalysis.conducted == true && BiasAnalysis.resultsDocumented == true
evidence_expected: bias impact assessment
requirements.source_quote: (f) examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations;

requirements.title: Implement measures to detect, prevent and mitigate identified biases
requirements.obligation: Apply appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate biases identified in the bias examination.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: BiasMitigation.measuresImplemented == true && BiasMitigation.efficacyEvaluated == true
evidence_expected: bias mitigation plan and effectiveness evaluation
requirements.source_quote: (g) appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f);

requirements.title: Identify and address data gaps or shortcomings
requirements.obligation: Identify relevant data gaps or shortcomings that prevent compliance and outline how they will be addressed.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataGapAnalysis.completed == true && DataGapRemediationPlan.available == true
evidence_expected: data‑gap analysis report
remediation action plan
requirements.source_quote: (h) the identification of relevant data gaps or shortcomings that prevent compliance with this Regulation, and how those gaps and shortcomings can be addressed.

requirements.title: Ensure relevance, representativeness, error‑freedom and completeness of data sets
requirements.obligation: Ensure training, validation and testing data sets are relevant, sufficiently representative, as error‑free as possible, complete for the intended purpose and possess appropriate statistical properties.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.relevant == true && DataSet.representative == true && DataSet.errorRate ≤ acceptableThreshold && DataSet.complete == true && DataSet.statisticalPropertiesSuitable == true
evidence_expected: data quality and representativeness report
statistical properties validation worksheet
requirements.source_quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose. They shall have the appropriate statistical properties, including, where applicable, as regards the persons or groups of persons in relation to whom the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.

requirements.title: Adapt data sets to specific geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional settings
requirements.obligation: Take into account, to the extent required by the intended purpose, characteristics specific to the geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of the intended use.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems using training, validation or testing data sets
requirements.machine_constraint: DataSet.contextualAdaptation.includes({geographical, contextual, behavioural, functional}) == true
evidence_expected: contextual adaptation analysis
requirements.source_quote: Data sets shall take into account, to the extent required by the intended purpose, the characteristics or elements that are particular to the specific geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting within which the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.

requirements.title: Limited applicability of data‑quality requirements to testing data sets for non‑training systems
requirements.obligation: When a high‑risk AI system does not use model‑training techniques, apply the requirements of Articles 10(2)‑(4) and Article 4a(1) only to the testing data sets.
requirements.actor: provider or developer of a high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: high‑risk AI systems that do NOT use techniques involving the training of AI models
requirements.machine_constraint: if System.usesTrainingTechniques == false then Requirements.applyTo == {testingDataSets}
evidence_expected: statement of non‑training nature of the system
compliance evidence limited to testing data sets
requirements.source_quote: For the development of high-risk AI systems not using techniques involving the training of AI models, paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of this Article and Article 4a(1) shall apply only to the testing data sets.

requirements.title: Automatic event recording over system lifetime
requirements.obligation: High‑risk AI systems must technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems as defined by the EU AI Act
requirements.machine_constraint: System shall generate immutable, tamper‑evident logs for every operational event from initial activation until decommissioning, without manual intervention.
evidence_expected: Log files covering the entire operational period
Metadata proving automatic generation (e.g., timestamps, system IDs)
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

requirements.title: Logging of events relevant to risk identification, post‑market monitoring and operational oversight
requirements.obligation: Logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for (a) identifying situations that may result in a risk or substantial modification, (b) facilitating post‑market monitoring, and (c) monitoring the operation of high‑risk AI systems referred to in Article 26(5).
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Log schema must include fields to capture risk‑triggering situations, post‑market monitoring data, and operational metrics required by Article 26(5), and must be searchable by these categories.
evidence_expected: Structured log entries indicating risk‑related events
Entries supporting post‑market monitoring activities
Operational monitoring records as defined in Article 26(5)
requirements.source_quote:
logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
(a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or in a substantial modification;
(b) facilitating the post-market monitoring referred to in Article 72; and
(c) monitoring the operation of high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 26(5).

requirements.title: Record of each usage period
requirements.obligation: Logging shall record the period of each use of the system (start date and time and end date and time of each use).
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems covered by point 1(a) of Annex III
requirements.machine_constraint: For every activation session, the system must write a log entry with fields: session_start_timestamp, session_end_timestamp, and a unique session identifier.
evidence_expected: Log entries listing start and end timestamps for each use session
requirements.source_quote: recording of the period of each use of the system (start date and time and end date and time of each use);

requirements.title: Record of reference database used for input verification
requirements.obligation: Logging shall capture the reference database against which input data has been checked by the system.
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems covered by point 1(a) of Annex III
requirements.machine_constraint: Log entries must include the identifier or version of the reference database employed for each verification operation.
evidence_expected: Log lines containing database name, version, or hash used during input validation
requirements.source_quote: the reference database against which input data has been checked by the system;

requirements.title: Record of input data that resulted in a match
requirements.obligation: Logging shall record the input data for which the search has led to a match.
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems covered by point 1(a) of Annex III
requirements.machine_constraint: For each successful match operation, the system must log a representation of the input data (e.g., hash or anonymised excerpt) that triggered the match.
evidence_expected: Log entries showing input data identifiers or hashes linked to matched outcomes
requirements.source_quote: the input data for which the search has led to a match;

requirements.title: Record of natural persons verifying results
requirements.obligation: Logging shall identify the natural persons involved in the verification of the results, as referred to in Article 14(5).
requirements.actor: Provider of the high‑risk AI system
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems covered by point 1(a) of Annex III
requirements.machine_constraint: Log entries must capture the unique identifier (e.g., employee ID) of each human verifier who reviews or validates system outputs.
evidence_expected: Log records linking verification actions to specific natural person identifiers
requirements.source_quote: the identification of the natural persons involved in the verification of the results, as referred to in Article 14(5).

requirements.title: Transparency by design and development
requirements.obligation: Design and develop the high‑risk AI system so that its operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret its output and use it appropriately.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: System architecture and accompanying documentation must contain explicit interpretability mechanisms (e.g., model‑explainability artefacts, output‑mapping logic) that can be accessed by deployers.
evidence_expected: Design documentation describing transparency measures
Interpretability artefact specifications
Transparency‑assessment report
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately.

requirements.title: Provision of user instructions in digital format
requirements.obligation: Accompany the high‑risk AI system with instructions for use in an appropriate digital format (or otherwise) that are concise, complete, correct, clear, relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Deliver an instruction package in a machine‑readable digital format (e.g., PDF/HTML/JSON) that includes required informational sections and meets accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG).
evidence_expected: Digital instruction file
Accessibility compliance statement
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate digital format or otherwise that include concise, complete, correct and clear information that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers.

requirements.title: Provider identity and contact details
requirements.obligation: Include the identity and contact details of the provider and, where applicable, of its authorised representative in the instructions for use.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Instruction set must contain fields: provider_name, provider_address, provider_email, representative_name (optional), representative_contact.
evidence_expected: Contact‑information section in the instruction document
requirements.source_quote: (a) the identity and the contact details of the provider and, where applicable, of its authorised representative;

requirements.title: Declared intended purpose
requirements.obligation: State the intended purpose of the high‑risk AI system.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Instructions must contain an 'intended_purpose' field describing the specific application(s) for which the system is designed.
evidence_expected: Purpose description in the instruction document
requirements.source_quote: (i) its intended purpose;

requirements.title: Performance metrics and robustness information
requirements.obligation: Provide the level of accuracy, associated metrics, robustness and cybersecurity information as tested and validated (per Article 15), together with any known or foreseeable circumstances that may impact these levels.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Instruction set must include a 'performance_metrics' object containing: accuracy_value, accuracy_metric, robustness_measures, cybersecurity_measures, test_conditions, and a 'known_circumstances' list.
evidence_expected: Performance‑metrics table
Test‑validation report
requirements.source_quote: (ii) the level of accuracy, including its metrics, robustness and cybersecurity referred to in Article 15 against which the high-risk AI system has been tested and validated and which can be expected, and any known and foreseeable circumstances that may have an impact on that expected level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity;

requirements.title: Risk scenarios related to misuse
requirements.obligation: Identify any known or foreseeable circumstances, related to use in accordance with the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable misuse, that may lead to risks to health, safety or fundamental rights (Article 9(2)).
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Include a 'risk_scenarios' list describing each circumstance, its likelihood, and potential impact on health, safety or fundamental rights.
evidence_expected: Risk‑scenario catalogue
Risk‑assessment documentation
requirements.source_quote: (iii) any known or foreseeable circumstance, related to the use of the high-risk AI system in accordance with its intended purpose or under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse, which may lead to risks to the health and safety or fundamental rights referred to in Article 9(2);

requirements.title: Technical characteristics for output explanation
requirements.obligation: Where applicable, describe the technical capabilities and characteristics that are relevant for explaining the system’s output.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Provide a 'technical_explanation' section detailing model type, feature importance methods, or rule sets used to generate outputs.
evidence_expected: Technical explanation documentation
requirements.source_quote: (iv) where applicable, the technical capabilities and characteristics of the high-risk AI system to provide information that is relevant to explain its output;

requirements.title: Performance for specific persons or groups
requirements.obligation: When appropriate, disclose the system’s performance regarding specific persons or groups of persons for which it is intended.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Include a 'group_performance' table with accuracy, false‑positive/negative rates, or other relevant metrics broken down by demographic group.
evidence_expected: Disaggregated performance report
requirements.source_quote: (v) when appropriate, its performance regarding specific persons or groups of persons on which the system is intended to be used;

requirements.title: Input‑data and training dataset specifications
requirements.obligation: When appropriate, provide specifications for the input data and any other relevant information about the training, validation and testing datasets used, considering the intended purpose.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Add an 'input_data_spec' section and a 'dataset_overview' object describing data sources, preprocessing, size, representativeness, and validation methodology.
evidence_expected: Dataset specification sheet
Data provenance records
requirements.source_quote: (vi) when appropriate, specifications for the input data, or any other relevant information in terms of the training, validation and testing data sets used, taking into account the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system;

requirements.title: Guidance to interpret system output
requirements.obligation: Where applicable, furnish information that enables deployers to interpret the output of the high‑risk AI system and use it appropriately.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Supply an 'output_interpretation_guide' detailing output formats, confidence scores, and recommended decision‑making steps.
evidence_expected: Interpretation guide document
requirements.source_quote: (vii) where applicable, information to enable deployers to interpret the output of the high-risk AI system and use it appropriately;

requirements.title: Pre‑determined changes and performance post‑conformity assessment
requirements.obligation: List any changes to the high‑risk AI system and its performance that were pre‑determined by the provider at the time of the initial conformity assessment.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Include a 'pre_determined_changes' catalogue documenting each change, its rationale, and expected performance impact.
evidence_expected: Change‑log annex to the instruction set
requirements.source_quote: (c) the changes to the high-risk AI system and its performance which have been pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment, if any;

requirements.title: Human‑oversight measures and interpretability aids
requirements.obligation: Describe the human‑oversight measures required by Article 14, including technical measures that facilitate deployers’ interpretation of the system’s outputs.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Provide a 'human_oversight' section enumerating oversight roles, intervention points, and any UI/visualisation tools that support output interpretation.
evidence_expected: Human‑oversight design description
requirements.source_quote: (d) the human oversight measures referred to in Article 14, including the technical measures put in place to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of the high-risk AI systems by the deployers;

requirements.title: Computational resources, lifetime and maintenance
requirements.obligation: Specify the computational and hardware resources required, the expected lifetime of the system, and any necessary maintenance and care measures (including frequency and software updates) to ensure proper functioning.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Add a 'resource_and_maintenance' module containing fields: cpu_requirements, gpu_requirements, storage, expected_lifetime_years, maintenance_schedule, update_policy.
evidence_expected: Resource specification sheet
Maintenance plan
requirements.source_quote: (e) the computational and hardware resources needed, the expected lifetime of the high-risk AI system and any necessary maintenance and care measures, including their frequency, to ensure the proper functioning of that AI system, including as regards software updates;

requirements.title: Logging mechanisms for collection, storage and interpretation
requirements.obligation: Where relevant, describe the mechanisms within the system that allow deployers to properly collect, store and interpret logs in accordance with Article 12.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Provide a 'logging_mechanism' description detailing log format, retention period, access controls, and tools for log analysis.
evidence_expected: Logging architecture diagram
Log‑management policy
requirements.source_quote: (f) where relevant, a description of the mechanisms included within the high-risk AI system that allows deployers to properly collect, store and interpret the logs in accordance with Article 12.

requirements.title: Design for effective human oversight
requirements.obligation: High‑risk AI systems shall be designed and developed so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use, including with appropriate human‑machine interface tools.
requirements.actor: Provider (designer / developer)
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must embed or expose human‑machine interface capabilities that enable a natural person to monitor and control the system effectively throughout its operational life.
evidence_expected: Design documentation describing oversight‑enabling features
User‑interface specifications
Verification test reports demonstrating effective human oversight
Technical files submitted to authorities
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.

requirements.title: Human oversight to prevent or minimise core risks
requirements.obligation: Human oversight shall aim to prevent or minimise risks to health, safety or fundamental rights that may emerge when a high‑risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose or under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse, especially where such risks persist despite other requirements.
requirements.actor: Provider and Deployer (through overseers)
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: The oversight process must target the mitigation of health, safety and fundamental‑rights risks that remain after application of other statutory safeguards.
evidence_expected: Risk‑assessment reports linking oversight measures to identified health/safety/fundamental‑rights risks
Procedures or guidelines for overseers describing risk‑prevention actions
requirements.source_quote: Human oversight shall aim to prevent or minimise the risks to health, safety or fundamental rights that may emerge when a high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose or under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse, in particular where such risks persist despite the application of other requirements set out in this Section.

requirements.title: Built‑in oversight measures (provider‑implemented)
requirements.obligation: When technically feasible, the provider shall identify and embed oversight measures into the high‑risk AI system before it is placed on the market or put into service.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems where technical feasibility allows embedding of oversight measures
requirements.machine_constraint: The system shall contain integrated functionalities (e.g., monitoring dashboards, alerts, safe‑stop mechanisms) that enable oversight without external add‑ons.
evidence_expected: Source code or firmware showing built‑in oversight functions
Technical documentation describing the integrated oversight features
Verification test results confirming operation of built‑in measures
requirements.source_quote: measures identified and built, when technically feasible, into the high-risk AI system by the provider before it is placed on the market or put into service

requirements.title: Provider‑identified oversight measures for deployer implementation
requirements.obligation: The provider shall identify oversight measures before placing the high‑risk AI system on the market or putting it into service that are appropriate to be implemented by the deployer.
requirements.actor: Provider (identification) and Deployer (implementation)
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: The provider must supply clear specifications of the oversight measures that the deployer must put in place (e.g., procedural controls, external monitoring tools).
evidence_expected: Oversight‑measure specification document delivered to the deployer
Implementation checklist or acceptance criteria for the deployer
requirements.source_quote: measures identified by the provider before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service and that are appropriate to be implemented by the deployer.

requirements.title: Enable overseer understanding, monitoring and bias awareness
requirements.obligation: The provider shall deliver the high‑risk AI system to the deployer in a manner that enables natural persons assigned to human oversight to properly understand the system’s capacities and limitations, monitor its operation (including detecting anomalies), and remain aware of automation bias.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Delivery must include documentation, training material, and interface features that convey system capabilities, limits, and bias‑awareness guidance.
evidence_expected: User manuals describing capacities and limitations
Training records on automation‑bias awareness
Monitoring dashboards or anomaly‑detection indicators
requirements.source_quote: to properly understand the relevant capacities and limitations of the high-risk AI system and be able to duly monitor its operation, including in view of detecting and addressing anomalies, dysfunctions and unexpected performance; to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)

requirements.title: Enable correct interpretation of system output
requirements.obligation: The provider shall equip overseers with appropriate tools and methods to correctly interpret the high‑risk AI system’s output.
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must be supplied together with interpretation tools, guidelines, or methods that facilitate accurate understanding of outputs.
evidence_expected: Interpretation tool specifications
Guidelines or decision‑support documentation
requirements.source_quote: to correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output, taking into account, for example, the interpretation tools and methods available

requirements.title: Empower overseers to reject or override system output
requirements.obligation: Oversight persons must be able, in any particular situation, to decide not to use the high‑risk AI system or to disregard, override or reverse its output.
requirements.actor: Deployer / Assigned natural persons
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: The system shall provide mechanisms (e.g., interface options, procedural rights) that allow overseers to bypass or reverse outputs without technical impediment.
evidence_expected: Interface screenshots showing override/reject functions
Procedural logs documenting instances of overridden outputs
requirements.source_quote: to decide, in any particular situation, not to use the high-risk AI system or to otherwise disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system

requirements.title: Safe‑stop capability for human intervention
requirements.obligation: Oversight persons must be able to intervene in the operation of the high‑risk AI system or interrupt it through a ‘stop’ button or similar procedure that brings the system to a safe state.
requirements.actor: Deployer / Assigned natural persons
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must incorporate a reliable, readily accessible stop or pause function that transitions the system to a safe state upon activation.
evidence_expected: Technical description of the stop mechanism
Testing reports demonstrating safe‑state transition
requirements.source_quote: to intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a ‘stop’ button or a similar procedure that allows the system to come to a halt in a safe state

requirements.title: Dual‑person verification for Annex III(1)(a) systems
requirements.obligation: For high‑risk AI systems referred to in point 1(a) of Annex III, no action or decision may be taken by the deployer on the basis of the system’s identification unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority.
requirements.actor: Deployer (with two qualified natural persons)
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems listed in Annex III point 1(a), except when used for law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum where Union or national law deems the requirement disproportionate.
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must support a verification workflow that records confirmation by two distinct, qualified persons before any decision based on the system’s output is executed.
evidence_expected: Audit logs showing signatures or IDs of two confirming persons
Workflow configuration enforcing dual‑person approval
requirements.source_quote: no action or decision is taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification resulting from the system unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority. The requirement for a separate verification by at least two natural persons shall not apply to high-risk AI systems used for the purposes of law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum, where Union or national law considers the application of this requirement to be disproportionate.

requirements.title: Design for appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout lifecycle
requirements.obligation: Design and develop high‑risk AI systems so that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity and maintain consistent performance in those respects throughout their lifecycle.
requirements.actor: Providers / developers of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: System shall meet defined thresholds for accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity and shall not degrade below those thresholds over the entire operational lifecycle.
evidence_expected: Design specification showing target accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity levels
Verification and validation test reports confirming thresholds are met
Lifecycle monitoring data demonstrating sustained performance
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

requirements.title: Commission to foster benchmarks and measurement methodologies
requirements.obligation: Encourage, as appropriate, the development of benchmarks and measurement methodologies for assessing accuracy and robustness of high‑risk AI systems.
requirements.actor: European Commission (in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and organisations such as metrology and benchmarking authorities)
requirements.applicability: Technical aspects of measuring appropriate levels of accuracy and robustness for high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Commission shall initiate or support activities leading to the creation of standardized benchmarks and measurement methods.
evidence_expected: Records of commissioned projects or funding calls for benchmark development
Published guidelines or standards resulting from the cooperation
requirements.source_quote: To address the technical aspects of how to measure the appropriate levels of accuracy and robustness set out in paragraph 1 and any other relevant performance metrics, the Commission shall, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and organisations such as metrology and benchmarking authorities, encourage, as appropriate, the development of benchmarks and measurement methodologies.

requirements.title: Declaration of accuracy levels and metrics in user instructions
requirements.obligation: Declare the levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high‑risk AI systems in the accompanying instructions of use.
requirements.actor: Providers / manufacturers of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: User documentation must contain explicit numeric accuracy values and the metrics used to obtain them.
evidence_expected: Copy of the instructions of use showing accuracy levels and metrics
Change‑log documenting updates to declared values
requirements.source_quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.

requirements.title: Implement technical and organisational resilience measures
requirements.obligation: Take technical and organisational measures to make high‑risk AI systems as resilient as possible to errors, faults or inconsistencies arising within the system or its operating environment, especially when interacting with natural persons or other systems.
requirements.actor: Providers / operators of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: System must incorporate fault‑tolerance, error‑handling and environmental‑robustness controls proportionate to identified risks.
evidence_expected: Risk assessment identifying error/fault scenarios
Design artefacts describing resilience mechanisms
Test reports demonstrating system behaviour under simulated fault conditions
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates, in particular due to their interaction with natural persons or other systems. Technical and organisational measures shall be taken in this regard.

requirements.title: Mitigate biased feedback loops in continuously learning systems
requirements.obligation: Develop continuously learning high‑risk AI systems so as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of biased outputs influencing future inputs (feedback loops) and address any such loops with appropriate mitigation measures.
requirements.actor: Providers of high‑risk AI systems that continue to learn after market placement
requirements.applicability: High‑risk AI systems that continue to learn post‑deployment
requirements.machine_constraint: Implement monitoring and control mechanisms that detect and limit bias propagation from system outputs back into training data, and apply predefined mitigation actions.
evidence_expected: Documentation of feedback‑loop mitigation architecture
Monitoring logs showing detection of biased outputs
Records of corrective actions applied to the learning pipeline
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or put into service shall be developed in such a way as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of possibly biased outputs influencing input for future operations (feedback loops), and as to ensure that any such feedback loops are duly addressed with appropriate mitigation measures.

requirements.title: Resilience against unauthorised alteration
requirements.obligation: Ensure high‑risk AI systems are resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
requirements.actor: Providers / operators of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Deploy security controls (e.g., integrity checks, access controls, tamper‑evidence mechanisms) that prevent or detect unauthorised modifications.
evidence_expected: Security architecture description
Penetration‑testing or vulnerability‑assessment reports
Logs of integrity‑verification events
requirements.source_quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.

requirements.title: Proportionate cybersecurity solutions
requirements.obligation: Select technical solutions ensuring the cybersecurity of high‑risk AI systems that are appropriate to the relevant circumstances and the risks.
requirements.actor: Providers of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: Conduct a risk assessment and implement cybersecurity measures whose strength is commensurate with identified risk levels.
evidence_expected: Risk assessment report linking identified threats to chosen security controls
Documentation of implemented cybersecurity measures
requirements.source_quote: The technical solutions aiming to ensure the cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems shall be appropriate to the relevant circumstances and the risks.

requirements.title: Countermeasures for AI‑specific vulnerabilities
requirements.obligation: Include, where appropriate, technical measures to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve and control attacks such as data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples/model evasion, confidentiality attacks and other model flaws.
requirements.actor: Providers of high‑risk AI systems
requirements.applicability: All high‑risk AI systems
requirements.machine_constraint: System shall incorporate detection and mitigation controls for each listed AI‑specific attack vector, proportionate to risk assessment outcomes.
evidence_expected: Security control specifications covering data‑poisoning, model‑poisoning, adversarial‑example detection, confidentiality safeguards, etc.
Test results demonstrating effectiveness against simulated attacks
Incident‑response procedures for identified AI‑specific threats
requirements.source_quote: The technical solutions to address AI specific vulnerabilities shall include, where appropriate, measures to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve and control for attacks trying to manipulate the training data set (data poisoning), or pre-trained components used in training (model poisoning), inputs designed to cause the AI model to make a mistake (adversarial examples or model evasion), confidentiality attacks or model flaws.

requirements.title: User notification for AI‑mediated interaction
requirements.obligation: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious …
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: All AI systems that directly interact with natural persons, except where the AI‑generated nature is obvious to a reasonably well‑informed, observant and circumspect person, and except for AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences (unless publicly available for reporting offences).
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must be capable of emitting a user‑facing notice (e.g., visual banner, spoken statement, or other modality) that explicitly states the interaction is with an AI system. The notice must be configurable to be suppressed only when a policy flag ‘obvious‑to‑user’ is set true, and must be omitted for law‑enforcement‑authorised systems.
evidence_expected: UI screenshot or video showing the AI interaction notice
Configuration file or flag indicating the ‘obvious‑to‑user’ condition
Documentation of exemption handling for law‑enforcement authorisation
requirements.source_quote: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use. This obligation shall not apply to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence.

requirements.title: Machine‑readable marking of synthetic content
requirements.obligation: Providers of AI systems … generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine‑readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Providers shall ensure their technical solutions are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable …
requirements.actor: Provider
requirements.applicability: All AI systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text, except when the system performs an assistive function for standard editing, does not substantially alter the input data/semantics, or is authorised by law for criminal‑offence detection, prevention, investigation or prosecution.
requirements.machine_constraint: Every generated artefact must carry a standardized metadata field (e.g., ‘synthetic‑flag: true’, conforming to a recognised technical standard) that can be programmatically read. The metadata must be embedded in the file format (EXIF, ID3, etc.) or attached as a separate machine‑readable manifest. The implementation must pass interoperability tests against at least two reference tools and meet defined reliability thresholds (e.g., >99% detection rate in test corpus).
evidence_expected: Sample generated files with the required metadata visible in a technical inspector
Interop test report showing successful detection by third‑party tools
Compliance report referencing the technical standard(s) used
requirements.source_quote: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Providers shall ensure their technical solutions are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as this is technically feasible, taking into account the specificities and limitations of various types of content, the costs of implementation and the generally acknowledged state of the art, as may be reflected in relevant technical standards. This obligation shall not apply to the extent the AI systems perform an assistive function for standard editing or do not substantially alter the input data provided by the deployer or the semantics thereof, or where authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences.

requirements.title: Transparency and data‑protection for emotion‑recognition and biometric categorisation
requirements.obligation: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system, and shall process the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable.
requirements.actor: Deployer
requirements.applicability: All deployments of emotion‑recognition or biometric‑categorisation systems, except when the system is permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences and appropriate safeguards are in place.
requirements.machine_constraint: The deployment environment must present a conspicuous notice (e.g., UI banner, audible alert) stating that emotion or biometric categorisation is occurring. Additionally, the system must log all personal‑data processing activities and expose them via an auditable API compliant with GDPR/ relevant EU data‑protection directives.
evidence_expected: Capture of the user‑facing notice displayed at system startup or point of capture
Exported processing log showing lawful basis, data categories, retention periods
Data‑protection impact assessment (DPIA) reference confirming compliance with GDPR, etc.
requirements.source_quote: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system, and shall process the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable. This obligation shall not apply to AI systems used for biometric categorisation and emotion recognition, which are permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, and in accordance with Union law.

requirements.title: Disclosure of AI‑generated deep‑fake visual/audio content
requirements.obligation: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
requirements.actor: Deployer
requirements.applicability: All deep‑fake image/audio/video generated or manipulated by AI, except where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offence, or where the content is part of an artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work – in which case only a limited disclosure of existence is required.
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must embed a verifiable disclosure indicator (e.g., visible overlay watermark or metadata tag ‘deep‑fake:true’) that can be automatically extracted. For artistic exceptions, the indicator may be limited to a non‑intrusive metadata field stating existence without visual alteration.
evidence_expected: Example deep‑fake file with visible watermark or metadata tag
Policy document describing handling of artistic‑exception content
Test script that extracts and confirms the disclosure flag
requirements.source_quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. This obligation shall not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offence. Where the content forms part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme, the transparency obligations set out in this paragraph are limited to disclosure of the existence of such generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work.

requirements.title: Disclosure of AI‑generated text of public‑interest
requirements.obligation: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated.
requirements.actor: Deployer
requirements.applicability: All AI‑generated or manipulated textual content published for public‑interest purposes, except where the use is authorised by law for criminal‑offence purposes, or where the content has undergone human review/editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility.
requirements.machine_constraint: Before publication, the content management workflow must append a clear editorial note or metadata flag (e.g., ‘AI‑generated:true’) that is programmatically accessible and displayed to end‑users. The workflow must also record whether human editorial oversight was applied, disabling the AI‑disclosure flag when appropriate.
evidence_expected: Published article excerpt showing the AI‑generation notice
CMS audit log indicating the AI‑disclosure flag state and editorial review record
Configuration showing the conditional disabling of the notice after editorial control
requirements.source_quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated. This obligation shall not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences or where the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication of the content.

requirements.title: Timing and accessibility of transparency information
requirements.obligation: The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure. The information shall conform to the applicable accessibility requirements.
requirements.actor: Provider or Deployer (whichever supplies the information)
requirements.applicability: All situations covered by paragraphs 1‑4.
requirements.machine_constraint: The system must render the required notice before or at the moment of first user interaction, using UI components that meet the EU accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG 2.2 Level AA). The notice must be programmatically distinguishable (e.g., ARIA role="alert").
evidence_expected: Screen‑reader test report confirming compliance with accessibility criteria
Timestamped log showing notice displayed prior to first user action
Design mock‑up of the clear and distinguishable notice
requirements.source_quote: The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure. The information shall conform to the applicable accessibility requirements.

requirements.title: Non‑prejudice of other transparency obligations
requirements.obligation: Paragraphs 1 to 4 shall not affect the requirements and obligations set out in Chapter III, and shall be without prejudice to other transparency obligations laid down in Union or national law for deployers of AI systems.
requirements.actor: All providers and deployers
requirements.applicability: Universal – any provider or deployer subject to Article 50.
requirements.machine_constraint: Compliance verification must cross‑check that implementations of Article 50 do not conflict with obligations in Chapter III or with any national transparency statutes; a compliance matrix mapping required notices to other legal duties is required.
evidence_expected: Compliance matrix linking Article 50 notices to Chapter III requirements
Legal review document confirming no conflict with national transparency laws
requirements.source_quote: Paragraphs 1 to 4 shall not affect the requirements and obligations set out in Chapter III, and shall be without prejudice to other transparency obligations laid down in Union or national law for deployers of AI systems.

requirements.title: Commission‑led codes of practice for detection, marking and labelling
requirements.obligation: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice … The Commission … shall assess whether adherence to those codes of practice is adequate to ensure compliance with the obligations laid down in paragraphs 2 and 4 … If it deems the code of practice to be inadequate, the Commission may adopt an implementing act …
requirements.actor: European Commission (with Board opinion)
requirements.applicability: All providers and deployers subject to the marking and labelling obligations of paragraphs 2 and 4.
requirements.machine_constraint: Systems must be capable of demonstrating conformity with any Commission‑adopted code of practice (e.g., by supporting the required metadata schema version indicated in the code). A compliance interface shall expose the code‑of‑practice version identifier and a self‑assessment attestation.
evidence_expected: Attestation document referencing the specific Commission code of practice version
Technical artifact (e.g., metadata schema file) showing alignment with the code
Record of Commission assessment outcome if available
requirements.source_quote: The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection, marking and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content. The Commission, taking utmost account of the opinion of the Board, shall assess whether adherence to those codes of practice is adequate to ensure compliance with the obligations laid down in paragraphs 2 and 4 of this Article, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 56(6). If it deems the code of practice to be inadequate, the Commission may adopt an implementing act specifying common rules for the implementation of those obligations in accordance with the examination procedure laid down in Article 98(2).
